service syncthing: network_mode: host networking has no equivalent: an Incus instance has a network namespace of its own and meets the host's network only through a NIC. What an app wants it for is usually to find devices on the LAN, or to be found there. The Incus answer is a NIC on the LAN's bridge (nictype bridged, parent the bridge, an address outside the router's DHCP pool), which is a decision about the site: tink writes none (docs/docker-to-tink.md says how; #206 proposes a way to declare the need). If the app only needed to be reached on a port, publish it. If an Incus network really is named host, add its NIC with --incus-device
